# Database and persistence

Persistence is a detail of the domain, not its centre. The schema changes only through migrations.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Profile `layered`

Layered monolith — Api, Application, Infrastructure, Domain, one project each.

### Rules

- **NET-005** · `arch-test` — A domain entity carries no persistence or serialisation attribute.
  Why: An attribute is a reference to a framework the domain is not allowed to know.
- **NET-006** · guidance — The relational mapping is declared in an `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` of the `Infrastructure` project.
  Why: One file per entity, next to the migrations, instead of a `DbContext` that grows without bound.
- **NET-007** · `arch-test` — A repository implementation is `internal`; the rest of the application sees only its interface.
  Why: A public implementation gets injected directly the day someone is in a hurry.

### Tables

`note`

| Column | Type | Nullable |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | identity | no |
| `title` | string(200) | no |
| `body` | text | no |
| `created_at` | timestamp | no |

### Adding a migration

From the root of the repository:

```bash
dotnet ef migrations add <Nom> \
  --project src/Edge.Api.Infrastructure \
  --startup-project src/Edge.Api.Api
```
